A.name: Team (Category, 20% of Overall)
A.definition: Weighted roll-up of A.1, A.2 and A.3.

A.1.a.name: Founder Education in the Field
A.1.a.definition: Highest relevant qualification and the standing of the institution, judged against whether this sector actually requires technical or regulatory literacy.
A.1.a.where_to_find: Not in the model — take from the pitch deck team page, LinkedIn, or the company's own bios.
A.1.a.if_missing: Mark Not Enough Information. Do not guess from a name or a photograph.

A.1.b.name: Founder Connections in the Field
A.1.b.definition: Count of marquee clients, partners or suppliers won specifically because of the founder's existing relationships. Named logos only.
A.1.b.where_to_find: Client list or revenue-by-customer tab; cross-reference against the deck's logo slide and ask which came via the founder.
A.1.b.if_missing: Fall back to the ANC_FDR_NETWORK anchors and say in DD Findings that the count could not be evidenced.

A.1.c.name: Founder and Co-Founder Relationship
A.1.c.definition: Years the founders have worked together or known each other, counted from first professional or academic overlap, not from incorporation.
A.1.c.where_to_find: Not in the model — founder bios, LinkedIn overlap, or ask directly in the management call.
A.1.c.if_missing: If there is only one founder, set the Evidence Tier to N/A so the weight is redistributed, and note that key-man risk sits under A.2.

A.1.d.name: Founder Years of Experience Within the Industry
A.1.d.definition: Years of full-time work in this industry before or during this venture. Adjacent-industry years count at half.
A.1.d.where_to_find: Not in the model — founder CV or LinkedIn. Take the earliest verifiable role in the sector.
A.1.d.if_missing: Mark Not Enough Information rather than inferring from age.

A.1.e.name: Any Previous Startup Experience
A.1.e.definition: Scored on the outcome of prior ventures, not the count — a realised exit or a scaled business is what separates the top band.
A.1.e.where_to_find: Not in the model — founder bio, LinkedIn, press. Verify any claimed exit independently.
A.1.e.if_missing: Score Poor only if you have positively established there is no startup exposure; otherwise mark Not Enough Information.

A.2.name: CXO Profiles / Other Leadership
A.2.definition: Weighted roll-up of the four leadership seats. Cross-check the result against TEAM_CXO_SEATS in Rubrics.

A.2.a.name: Product / Tech Leadership in Place
A.2.a.definition: Is there a full-time, credible owner of product and technology, and has that person built the function at the next stage of scale?
A.2.a.where_to_find: Headcount or payroll tab — look for the role, the salary band and the start date. Confirm against the deck's team page.
A.2.a.if_missing: If the seat is not mentioned anywhere, treat it as vacant and score Poor — absence is itself the finding. Say so in DD Findings.

A.2.b.name: Sales / GTM Leadership in Place
A.2.b.definition: Full-time owner of revenue. In a founder-led-sales company, ask whether the founder is still the only closer.
A.2.b.where_to_find: Headcount or payroll tab; also check whether the sales plan in the model assumes hires not yet made.
A.2.b.if_missing: As above — treat an unmentioned seat as vacant, not as unknown.

A.2.c.name: Finance Leadership in Place
A.2.c.definition: Full-time finance owner. The quality of the model you are reading is itself evidence — a clean, driver-based model implies real finance capability.
A.2.c.where_to_find: Headcount tab; and judge the model's own construction quality. Ask who built it.
A.2.c.if_missing: A model built by the founder or an outside consultant, with no in-house finance lead, is Fair at best.

A.2.d.name: Operations Leadership in Place
A.2.d.definition: Full-time owner of delivery, supply chain or service operations — whichever is the operational core of this business.
A.2.d.where_to_find: Headcount tab; check against the operational build-up driving COGS in the model.
A.2.d.if_missing: As above. In an ops-heavy business a vacant ops seat should also be raised as a risk in DD Findings.

A.3.name: Board / Advisors / Investors
A.3.definition: Weighted roll-up of A.3.a, A.3.b and A.3.c.

A.3.a.name: Formal Board in Place
A.3.a.definition: Existence, composition and actual functioning of the board — frequency, packs, minutes, and whether an independent voice exists.
A.3.a.where_to_find: Not in the model — shareholders' agreement, board minutes, or the management call.
A.3.a.if_missing: Mark Not Enough Information; do not assume a board exists because investors are on the cap table.

A.3.b.name: Marquee / Credible Advisors
A.3.b.definition: Count of advisors with senior domain standing who are actively engaged — documented cadence or equity/fees at stake.
A.3.b.where_to_find: Cap table (advisor equity or ESOP grants) and the deck's advisor slide.
A.3.b.if_missing: Count only those you can evidence. Website logos with no arrangement score Poor, not Not Enough Information.

A.3.c.name: Nature of Investors
A.3.c.definition: Count of institutional investors on the cap table, then sense-checked against investor quality and cap-table cleanliness. Non-standard terms cap this at Fair.
A.3.c.where_to_find: Cap table tab — shareholding by holder, instrument type, and any liquidation preference or veto rights.
A.3.c.if_missing: If no cap table is provided, that is a material gap: mark Not Enough Information and raise it as a diligence request.

B.name: Financials (Category, 20% of Overall)
B.definition: Weighted roll-up of B.1 to B.9.

B.1.name: Scale of Revenue
B.1.definition: Annualised net revenue run-rate = latest full month's net revenue × 12. Net of discounts, returns and GST. Never use GMV or gross booking value.
B.1.where_to_find: Calculated — B. Financials §3.1 row 29 (Net Revenue), annualised on months in row 23
B.1.if_missing: If only annual figures exist, use the last completed financial year and say so. Never annualise a forecast month.

B.2.name: Revenue Growth
B.2.definition: (Current year net revenue / prior year net revenue) − 1, on actuals only. Where a part-year is involved, compare like periods.
B.2.where_to_find: Calculated — B. Financials §3.4 row 74. Stays blank until the §3.5 revenue triangulation passes
B.2.if_missing: With under two years of history, use the trailing 6 months annualised vs the prior 6 months and label it as such.

B.3.name: Gross Margin Profile, CM1
B.3.definition: (Net revenue − direct COGS − fulfilment/delivery cost) / net revenue. Excludes marketing, salaries and overhead.
B.3.if_missing: If the cost split cannot be established, mark Not Enough Information — do not use reported gross profit if its composition is unclear.

B.4.name: CM2
B.4.definition: CM1 less variable marketing and customer acquisition cost, as a percentage of net revenue. This is the unit-economics test.
B.4.if_missing: If marketing cannot be split into fixed and variable, treat all of it as variable and flag the conservatism in DD Findings.

B.5.name: EBITDA
B.5.definition: EBITDA / net revenue, on actuals. Add back non-cash ESOP charges and genuine one-offs; list every adjustment made.
B.5.if_missing: Never take a founder-adjusted or 'normalised' EBITDA at face value. Rebuild it and show the bridge.

B.6.name: PAT
B.6.definition: Profit after tax / net revenue, on actuals. A wide EBITDA-to-PAT gap points to leverage, heavy depreciation or a tax issue — explain which.
B.6.if_missing: If only management accounts exist, say so — unaudited PAT carries less weight and should be noted.

B.7.name: Burn Rate / Runway Available
B.7.definition: Runway = closing cash and equivalents / trailing 3-month average net monthly burn, measured pre-money. Burn multiple = net burn over the period / net new revenue added over the same period.
B.7.if_missing: If the company is EBITDA-positive and cash generative, enter a runway above the Excellent cut and note that it is self-funding. Short runway must also be reflected in D.8 Seller Motivation.

B.8.name: Working Capital
B.8.definition: Inventory days + receivable days − payable days, each computed on the trailing 12 months. Negative is excellent — the business funds itself on float.
B.8.if_missing: For a pure-services or pre-revenue business, set inventory to zero. If the balance sheet is absent, mark Not Enough Information.

B.9.name: Debt
B.9.definition: Total interest-bearing debt / annualised net revenue. Include venture debt, working-capital lines drawn, lease liabilities and any CCD treated as debt.
B.9.if_missing: Where EBITDA is positive, also compute FIN_DEBT_EBITDA and score on the worse of the two. Zero debt scores Excellent.

C.name: Business Quality (Category, 10% of Overall)
C.definition: Weighted roll-up of C.1 to C.8.

C.1.name: How Many Years Since Started
C.1.definition: Years from incorporation to today. Range-scored: too young to have proof, or old enough that the absence of scale is itself the finding.
C.1.where_to_find: Not in the model — incorporation certificate, MCA record, or the deck. Use operating start date if it differs materially and say which you used.
C.1.if_missing: Read alongside B.1 for the same stage — an old company at seed-scale revenue should score poorly on both.

C.2.name: Revenue Predictability
C.2.definition: Share of revenue that is contracted, subscription or AMC with at least 12 months' visibility. Repeat transactional revenue counts at half weight — state the treatment used.
C.2.where_to_find: Revenue-by-type or revenue-by-customer tab; contract schedule if provided. Check whether the model's forecast assumes renewal rates it has not earned.
C.2.if_missing: If revenue cannot be split by type, estimate from customer repeat behaviour and label it an estimate. Also capture churn for BQ_CHURN.

C.3.name: Competitive Advantage / Moat
C.3.definition: Weighted roll-up of the five moat sub-items. Do not average them in your head — score each separately and let the sheet roll it up.

C.3.a.name: Proprietary IP / Technology
C.3.a.definition: Granted or filed IP central to the product, or a proprietary data asset. Judge on replication time by a well-funded competitor, not on the existence of a filing.
C.3.a.where_to_find: Not in the model — IP schedule, patent filings, the deck's technology slide. Check what is licensed in versus built.
C.3.a.if_missing: A patent that is not central to the product, or one nobody would enforce, is not a moat. Score Fair at best and say why.

C.3.b.name: Network Effects
C.3.b.definition: Does each additional user improve the product for the others? Tested against cohort retention improving and CAC falling as the base grows.
C.3.b.where_to_find: Cohort tab if present; marketing spend and new-customer counts by period to derive the CAC trend.
C.3.b.if_missing: A network-effects claim alongside rising CAC must be rejected. Most businesses have no network effects — Poor is the honest default.

C.3.c.name: Strong Brand
C.3.c.definition: Share of new customers arriving organically — direct, organic search, or referral. Excludes anything paid for.
C.3.c.where_to_find: Marketing or funnel tab — new customers by channel. Cross-check against the marketing spend line.
C.3.c.if_missing: If channel data is absent, use the ANC_MOAT_BRAND anchors and mark the number as unavailable.

C.3.d.name: Customer Stickiness
C.3.d.definition: Net revenue retention over 12 months: revenue this year from last year's cohort / revenue last year from that cohort, including expansion and churn.
C.3.d.where_to_find: Cohort or revenue-by-customer tab. If only logo retention is given, state that instead of passing it off as NRR.
C.3.d.if_missing: Rebuild NRR from the customer-level revenue table if it is not reported. If neither exists, mark Not Enough Information.

C.3.e.name: Scale / Cost Advantage
C.3.e.definition: Cost per delivered unit versus the largest named peer, expressed as a percentage difference. Negative means cheaper. Distinguish structural advantage from negotiated terms.
C.3.e.where_to_find: Unit economics tab; derive from COGS divided by units delivered. Peer cost must come from research or filings — cite it.
C.3.e.if_missing: Without a credible peer cost benchmark, use the anchors and mark the number unavailable. Do not invent a peer figure.

C.4.name: Scalability
C.4.definition: Annualised net revenue / total headcount, including contract staff. The test is whether revenue grows faster than headcount.
C.4.where_to_find: Headcount or payroll tab for the denominator; P&L for revenue. Check the model's forecast — does it assume headcount scales linearly with revenue?
C.4.if_missing: If headcount is not given, derive it from total payroll divided by an assumed average salary and label it an estimate.

C.5.name: Pricing Power
C.5.definition: Year-on-year change in gross margin, in basis points, as the pricing-power proxy. Supported by any realised price increase taken in the last 12 months.
C.5.where_to_find: P&L tab — compute CM1 for both years and take the difference. Price changes usually sit in the revenue build or a pricing tab.
C.5.if_missing: Credit a price increase only after checking churn in the following two quarters. A rise taken with customers walking out is not pricing power.

C.6.name: Low Client / Segment Concentration
C.6.definition: Combined revenue share of the five largest customers over the trailing 12 months. Capture the largest single customer separately.
C.6.where_to_find: Revenue-by-customer tab. If customers are anonymised, use the ranked revenue table.
C.6.if_missing: If the top-1 score is two bands worse than top-5, override C.6 down and explain — single-client risk is the real exposure.

C.7.name: Supplier Concentration
C.7.definition: Largest single supplier's share of total COGS over the trailing 12 months.
C.7.where_to_find: Purchase or vendor tab; otherwise the COGS build-up. Check the notes for exclusivity or sole-source arrangements.
C.7.if_missing: Score worse than the raw number implies if the supplier is also a competitor, sole-source, or an exclusive import agent — and say so.

C.8.name: Low Government Regulation
C.8.definition: Licensing burden, price control, subsidy dependence and pending adverse legislation. This is the only place regulation is scored.
C.8.where_to_find: Not in the model — licences held and renewal dates, the relevant regulator, pending legislation, any live litigation.
C.8.if_missing: Do not double-count regulation under E. Sector — the news-flow sub-items there cover sentiment only.

D.name: Deal Dynamics (Category, 10% of Overall)
D.definition: Weighted roll-up of D.1 to D.8.

D.1.name: Current Fund Raise / Last Fund Raise
D.1.definition: Current round size / previous round size, both in the same currency. Range-scored: a sensible step-up shows progress; too small signals a bridge, too large an unearned ask.
D.1.where_to_find: Funding history tab or cap table; the current ask is usually on the deck's 'the ask' slide.
D.1.if_missing: If this is the first institutional round, set the Evidence Tier to N/A so the weight redistributes — do not score it Poor.

D.2.name: Current Fund Raise / Total Fund Raise
D.2.definition: Current round / cumulative capital raised to date, as a percentage. Supported by current raise / annualised revenue, which sizes the ask against the business that exists today.
D.2.where_to_find: Cap table and funding history for cumulative capital; P&L for revenue.
D.2.if_missing: If prior funding is bootstrapped or negligible, note it and score on DD_RAISE_TO_ARR instead.

D.3.name: Existing Investor Contribution
D.3.definition: Share of the current round committed by existing investors. The strongest conviction signal available — insiders know most.
D.3.where_to_find: Term sheet or the deck's round-structure slide; confirm in the management call who has committed and how firmly.
D.3.if_missing: Distinguish soft indications from signed commitments. Zero insider participation should force a hard look at D.8.

D.4.name: Low Valuation Expectation Sensitivity
D.4.definition: Implied EV/Revenue on the ask, expressed as a percentage premium to the sub-sector median multiple. A discount is excellent.
D.4.where_to_find: Valuation ask from the deck; peer multiples from research or filings. Cross-check ticket sizes in Sector Deal Data.
D.4.if_missing: If no peer multiple can be established, score on the ANC_VAL_FLEX anchors — how the founder holds the number matters as much as the number.

D.5.name: Founder Dilution Level to Date
D.5.definition: Founders' combined shareholding immediately after this round, fully diluted including ESOP pool. Expressed as remaining stake so higher is better.
D.5.where_to_find: Cap table — use the fully diluted post-money column. If it does not exist, build it from the pre-money table and the round size.
D.5.if_missing: Below the Fair cut, founder incentives are impaired and the next round gets harder — raise it in DD Findings even if everything else is strong.

D.6.name: Founder Does Not Think He is the Banker
D.6.definition: Count of investors the founder has already approached directly. A shopped deal is a damaged deal — every burnt name is one we cannot take to market.
D.6.where_to_find: Not in the model — ask directly in the management call and ask for the list in writing.
D.6.if_missing: If the founder will not provide the list, that is itself a Poor signal on the anchors. Note the refusal.

D.7.name: Use of Proceeds
D.7.definition: Share of proceeds going to growth — capex, hiring, market entry, product. Excludes funding existing losses, repaying debt and buying out shareholders.
D.7.where_to_find: Use-of-proceeds slide, cross-checked against the model's forecast cash flows — does the plan actually spend the money the way the slide says?
D.7.if_missing: Where the slide and the model disagree, score on the model and flag the divergence. Any secondary component must be disclosed here.

D.8.name: Seller Motivation
D.8.definition: Why they are raising now, how specific and time-bound the reason is, whether the board has approved it, and whether the timetable is being set by the bank balance.
D.8.where_to_find: Not in the model — management call. Cross-check the stated reason against runway from B.7 and the use of proceeds in D.7.
D.8.if_missing: Runway under 6 months caps this at Fair however good the story. An undisclosed motive discovered later is the single most damaging surprise in a mandate.

E.name: Sector Attractiveness (Category, 10% of Overall)
E.definition: Weighted roll-up of E.1 to E.7. Select the sector name in E. Sector!C2 first — three parameters populate themselves from Sector Deal Data.

E.1.name: Market Size & Growth (TAM / SAM / SOM)
E.1.definition: India-addressable TAM and the forward market CAGR, each banded separately against the stage rubric. The two scores are averaged and re-banded, so a large market growing slowly and a small market growing fast both land mid-table. If only one of the two is captured, that one carries the row.
E.1.where_to_find: Not in the model — industry research, rating-agency or regulator reports. Cite the source and the build-up method.
E.1.if_missing: Reject a TAM built by multiplying the population by a price. If only a global TAM is available, scale it to India and say how.

E.2.name: Velocity of Deals in Sector
E.2.definition: Deal-count percentile across the 18 sectors, blended across the sectors selected on E. Sector C19:C21 at 100% / 67-33% / 50-30-20%. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute deal-count floor on Deal Scorecard L76:L78.
E.2.where_to_find: Nothing to enter — the lookup does it. Just confirm the sector name in C2 is the right one.
E.2.if_missing: If it does not populate, the sector name does not match the database list. Pick the closest listed sector; do not overwrite the formula.

E.3.name: Ticket Size of Deals
E.3.definition: Average-ticket percentile across the 18 sectors, blended on the same sector weights. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute ticket floor on Deal Scorecard L82:L84.
E.3.where_to_find: Nothing to enter. Do sense-check the deal size in G.5 against this — a raise far above sector norms will be hard to place.
E.3.if_missing: As above — fix the sector name, never the formula.

E.4.name: Tenor of Top Peer, Top 3 Peers
E.4.definition: Average age in years of the three largest peers. Established peers prove the category is real and give acquirers a reference point.
E.4.where_to_find: Not in the model — name the three peers, then take incorporation years from MCA or company records.
E.4.if_missing: Name the peers you used in DD Findings. A category with no identifiable peers is a finding in itself.

E.5.name: Top 3 Peers Last Capital Raise
E.5.definition: Months since the most recent capital raise among the top three peers. Recent raises mean live investor appetite; stale raises mean the category has gone quiet.
E.5.where_to_find: Not in the model — Sector Deal Data for recorded deals, plus press and filings for anything more recent.
E.5.if_missing: If no peer has ever raised institutional capital, that is a serious GTM risk — score Poor and say so explicitly.

E.6.name: Number of Investors in the Sector
E.6.definition: Unique-investor percentile across the 18 sectors, blended on the same sector weights. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute investor floor on Deal Scorecard L79:L81.
E.6.where_to_find: Nothing to enter — populates from the sector name.
E.6.if_missing: Cross-check against IB_INVESTOR_RELS: a sector with many active investors but no warm relationships for us is a G.1 problem, not an E problem.

E.7.name: News Flow & Sentiment
E.7.definition: Weighted roll-up of the two news sub-items. Folded in from the former standalone News Flow sheet; its government-regulation item was dropped to avoid double-counting C.8.

E.7.a.name: News of Peers in Sector
E.7.a.definition: Count of positive funding, expansion or acquisition events involving named peers in the last six months. Count distinct events, not distinct articles.
E.7.a.where_to_find: Not in the model — news search on the named peers, plus Sector Deal Data for recorded rounds.
E.7.a.if_missing: If peer news is materially negative — shutdowns, down rounds, fraud — score Poor on the anchors regardless of the count, and list the events.

E.7.b.name: News of Sector
E.7.b.definition: Ratio of positive to negative sector news events over the last six months. Below 1.0x the sector is generating more bad news than good.
E.7.b.where_to_find: Not in the model — sector news search over a defined six-month window. State the window and cite the sources.
E.7.b.if_missing: Judge on substance, not volume: one regulatory shock outweighs ten funding announcements. Explain the call in DD Findings.

F.name: Sub-Sector Attractiveness (Category, 20% of Overall)
F.definition: Weighted roll-up of F.1 to F.6. Carries double the weight of E because the sub-sector is where the deal actually competes — be more rigorous here, not less.

F.1.name: Market Size & Growth (TAM / SAM / SOM)
F.1.definition: India-addressable sub-sector TAM and its forward CAGR, each banded separately against the stage rubric, then averaged and re-banded. The sub-sector TAM must be materially smaller than the sector TAM.
F.1.where_to_find: Not in the model — sub-sector research. If your sub-sector TAM equals your sector TAM, one of the two is wrong.
F.1.if_missing: Same rules as E.1. Cite the source and the build-up.

F.2.name: Velocity of Deals in Sub-Sector
F.2.definition: Deal-count percentile across the 50 clubbed sub-sector groups. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute deal-count floor on Deal Scorecard L76:L78.
F.2.where_to_find: Nothing to enter. The database maps 104 raw sub-sectors into 50 clubbed groups — pick the clubbed group name.
F.2.if_missing: If the name does not match, consult the raw-to-clubbed mapping in Sector Deal Data columns L:P and use the clubbed group.

F.3.name: Ticket Size of Deals
F.3.definition: Average-ticket percentile across the 50 clubbed sub-sector groups. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute ticket floor.
F.3.where_to_find: Nothing to enter. This is the most relevant benchmark for sizing the raise in G.5.
F.3.if_missing: As F.2 — fix the name, never the formula.

F.4.name: Tenor of Top Peer, Top 3 Peers
F.4.definition: Average age of the three largest sub-sector peers — the direct competitors, not the broad sector leaders.
F.4.where_to_find: Not in the model — name the three direct competitors and take their incorporation years.
F.4.if_missing: The peers named here should differ from those in E.4. If they are identical, the sub-sector has been defined too broadly.

F.5.name: Top 3 Peers Last Capital Raise
F.5.definition: Months since the most recent raise among the three direct sub-sector peers.
F.5.where_to_find: Sector Deal Data plus press and filings for the named competitors.
F.5.if_missing: Same rules as E.5. A sub-sector where nobody has raised in two years is a hard GTM problem.

F.6.name: Number of Investors in the Sub-Sector
F.6.definition: Unique-investor percentile across the 50 clubbed sub-sector groups. Banded as the better of the percentile band and the absolute investor floor.
F.6.where_to_find: Nothing to enter — populates from the sub-sector name.
F.6.if_missing: A low count here with a high count in E.6 means capital is in the sector but not in this niche — an important distinction for GTM.

G.name: Mandate Context (Category, 10% of Overall)
G.definition: Weighted roll-up of G.1 to G.5. This category is about us, not the company — our ability to execute the mandate and get paid for it.

G.1.name: Sector Knowledge, Relationships
G.1.definition: Deals we have closed in this sector in the last three years, supported by the count of warm investor relationships active in the sub-sector.
G.1.where_to_find: Internal — our own deal log and investor CRM. Closed deals only; mandates that did not complete do not build a track record.
G.1.if_missing: This is our own information, so Not Enough Information is not an acceptable answer. Establish it.

G.2.name: GTM Timeline
G.2.definition: Weeks from mandate signing to being in market with materials. Driven by data-room readiness, audit quality and how much of the model we have to rebuild.
G.2.where_to_find: Judged from the quality of the pack you have just read — an unauditable model or missing statements adds weeks.
G.2.if_missing: Base this on the pack in front of you, not on the founder's timetable. Past 12 weeks the company is not raise-ready.

G.3.name: Realistic Timeline to Close Deal
G.3.definition: Months from launch to money in the bank, on a realistic rather than a best case. Larger, later deals legitimately take longer.
G.3.where_to_find: Judgement, informed by E.5/F.5 peer raise recency, the investor count, and deal size against sub-sector norms.
G.3.if_missing: Do not use the founder's expected close date. If our estimate and his differ materially, that gap belongs in DD Findings.

G.4.name: Capacity Available
G.4.definition: Live mandates per senior banker at the point of taking this on. Capacity is a real constraint on outcome, not an afterthought.
G.4.where_to_find: Internal — current live mandate list and who would actually run this one.
G.4.if_missing: Our own information — establish it. Name the banker who would own the deal.

G.5.name: Deal Size
G.5.definition: Capital being raised, in US$ Mn at the workbook FX rate. Scored against mandate economics — below the Fair cut the fee will not cover the effort.
G.5.where_to_find: The ask, from the deck or term sheet. Convert at ₹94 = US$1 (US$ Mn × 9.4 = INR Cr).
G.5.if_missing: Sense-check against the sub-sector average ticket in F.3 — an ask far above sub-sector norms will be hard to place regardless of quality.
